precepts.text: Now some of you are saying, she is all jacked up though. Here is the surprise: a wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man, but a godly woman is given to him that feareth the Lord. So ask yourself, why was she given to me? What am I not reflecting on, how am I not being real with myself, to understand why I am in the situation I am in? You see all of her flaws and you look at yourself like you never did anything wrong.
precepts.point: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun. Which he hath given thee: brothers, the Lord gave her to you. That sister was created for you. This is your portion all the days of your life.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Brothers, who gave her to you? The Lord did. Look at your wife: that sister was created for you. “for that is thy portion in this life”.

Now some of you are saying, God did that? She all jacked up, though. Here is another surprise: “A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that feareth the Lord.” Nobody here wrote the Bible. That is what the scripture says.

So ask yourself, why is she jacked up? Because you're jacked up; she was created just for you. Brothers see all of her flaws, all of her issues, every problem she has, and look at themselves like they never did anything wrong. Ask yourself: why was she given to me? What am I doing, what am I not reflecting on, how am I not being real with myself, to understand why I am in the situation I am in?

precepts.text: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord. If you are not serious about this walk, how can you expect a righteous woman? Everybody says I want that virtuous woman, but you have been in sin the whole time you have been in this truth and you want the Proverbs 31. No sir; that is not your portion. It goes according to where your faith is at. Now it is not always the case; sometimes a husband is righteous and he is trying to correct his wife and get her right.
precepts.point: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun. Which he hath given thee: brothers, the Lord gave her to you. That sister was created for you. This is your portion all the days of your life.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
“A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord.” A good wife is given to him that deserves a good wife: to them that fear the Lord. She is the portion Solomon spoke of in Ecclesiastes 9:9.

So think about this, brothers. If you are not serious about this walk in this truth, not serious about what you are supposed to be doing, how could you expect a righteous woman? Everybody says, I want that virtuous woman. But you nasty. You have been committing adultery since you have been in the truth, and you want the Proverbs 31? No, sir. You get the scum, the bottom of the barrel. Why? Because of where your faith is at.

Now, let's be real: it is not always the case. Sisters will say, well, if I messed up, that means you messed up. No. Sometimes a husband is trying to get you right. Sometimes he is trying to correct you, trying to show you what he wants so that you can be who he wants you to be. It ain't always him.

precepts.text: Here is the reality check for the evil sisters who think, if I am evil he must be evil, we will just be evil together. I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. A man will be delivered from a woman like that. So do not think you can just stay evil and you two will be together forever; the Lord will deliver him. How about you just repent and get it together so you can be heirs together.
precepts.point: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun. Which he hath given thee: brothers, the Lord gave her to you. That sister was created for you. This is your portion all the days of your life.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
Here is the reality check for the evil sisters who think, well, if I'm evil, he's evil, we're just going to be evil together. Solomon says: “And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart is snares and nets, and her hands as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her”.

Whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her. A man will be delivered from that type of woman. He will escape; he will get away.

So, sisters, don't think you can just be evil and die that way and the two of you will be together forever. No. The Lord will deliver him. How about we just repent and get our stuff together, so you can be heirs together? The wife the Lord gave is meant to be lived with joyfully all the days of your life, as a portion, not as a snare.

precepts.text: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun. That takes application; living joyfully is something you have to make happen. This woman, this rib, was made for you: that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.
precepts.point: This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Just as he had dominion over the other creatures, he had dominion over the woman: he named her. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” A help meet is someone to help him through his daily chores and through living, something to his liking, something for him. God first brought every beast and fowl to Adam, and Adam named them all, because he was over them. Then it says, “but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Nothing yet was just for him.

So “the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam”, took one of his ribs, “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” This is the Most High doing this for his son, and that is a gift. The gift still remains today for every man. That is why we call her your rib: there is a woman made just for you, because it is not good for man to be alone.

Solomon says what to do with that gift: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Living joyfully takes application. It is something you have to make happen.

He goes on: “for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” God made this woman for you. She is the portion you have been given in this life and in all the work you do under the sun, so receive her as the gift she is and live joyfully with her.

precepts.text: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, for that is thy portion. There is your romance, part of the aging, and it is a commandment; we are here seventy or eighty years at best.
precepts.point: He took her uprightly and they aged together mercifully, and with age comes beauty, love, and passion, not whimsical movie feelings. Stop chasing a feeling; get your mind like Tobit's. If even a majority of families moved in that spirit, how much stronger are we as a people for the time of trouble to come. Weddings are not done here for anyone who has not proved for three years.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.why:
Tobias prayed, “mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.” To age together is the long, intertwined journey of partners growing old side by side: shared history, mutual support through life's changes, companionship, and facing life's challenges as a team. Aged means refined, like wine or cheese.

Then Solomon: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity”. There's your romance. Live joyfully: that's part of the aging. “all the days of the life of thy vanity”, because we are here just for a fleeting moment, seventy or eighty years at best. All the days God gives you, you should live joyfully with your wife. That's a commandment.

“for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” This is how things are supposed to be set up. If you want to navigate this world the right way, you have to navigate your marriage this way.

So the joy is not the foundation; it grows out of it. Everything else has to be established first, or the romance will be fleeting and break the foundation of the scriptures. Tobias took his wife uprightly, and the living joyfully comes in the aging together.

precepts.point: Teaching the Law had a real effect on the nations; wisdom disarmed his enemies.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.”

Wisdom disarmed Jehoshaphat's enemies. He did not win by weapons of war; the fear of the Lord fell on the kingdoms round about, “so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.”

precepts.text: A poor wise man by his wisdom delivered a little city besieged by a great king.
precepts.point: Teaching the Law had a real effect on the nations; wisdom disarmed his enemies.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 17: Jehoshaphat Sends Teachers Through the Cities

precepts.why:
“There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city.”

Wisdom delivers where strength cannot. Judah taught the law in all its cities, and the fear of the Lord fell upon the kingdoms round about, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat. Wisdom disarmed his enemies.

precepts.text: There is no work and no devices in the grave; you cannot serve God when you are dead.
precepts.point: He asks whether His wonders shall be known in the dark and His righteousness in the land of forgetfulness. You can't serve God when you're dead.

note.label: Psalm 88: A Soul Full of Troubles

precepts.why:
The psalmist asks, “Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? shall the dead arise and praise thee?” and “Shall thy wonders be known in the dark? and thy righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?” Solomon answers why he pleads for his life now: “Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.”

There is no work and no device in the grave. You can't serve God when you're dead. That is why the psalmist begs to be heard while he lives: his lovingkindness is not declared in the grave, nor his faithfulness in destruction. Whatever your hand finds to do for the Most High, do it with your might while you have breath.

points: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of thy vanity: do not neglect her after the birth; make sure she gets the right food and is not in the house alone all the time, and have someone watch the children now and then, or she is overwhelmed and that brings on depression.

She was eight and a half months pregnant on a ladder painting the kitchen, he shouted, she cried; the hormones and the emotion are real, and the man has to be patient and apologise, but a sister cannot use her hormones to be evil or disrespectful.

points: The heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live. If it is not of God, it is madness. There is something about being here in this flesh: if you feel the pressure driving you to frustration and anger, the scripture already told you pressure will do that. Do not act on it.

Knowing that this is the condition of our flesh, you have to acknowledge that we have a tendency to drift. It is what the body does; it is what carnal mindedness does. It does not always manifest as rebellion. Rebellion is the escalation, the next level: when you give in to the drift, that is when you go into rebellion, a willful way of saying, I know that is wrong, but I am going to do it.
